items.title: Suno loses German copyright case, ordered to pay damages
points: A Munich court ruled AI music generator Suno processed songs without authorization during training and must pay damages.
The court found copyright violation regardless of the generative purpose of the AI.
Gema, the German rights organization, called it 'a verdict of global significance' that could sway courts worldwide.
Suno plans to appeal, but the ruling sets precedent that AI music tools need licensing to train on copyrighted works.

items.title: Gemini Spark becomes an errand runner inside Chrome
points: Google's Gemini Spark can now book apartment viewings, research flights, and start bookings using your saved passwords and logged-in accounts.
It requires explicit permission and hands payment decisions back to the user.
This puts AI agents (software that takes multi-step actions autonomously) into consumer Chrome workflows that previously required manual tab-switching and form-filling.

items.title: Four platforms, including Snapchat, downrank pure AI-generated video
points: Snapchat's Spotlight now deprioritizes wholly AI-generated videos in recommendations, while human-created, AI-edited content still appears.
Four platforms made the move within two weeks, signaling user fatigue with obvious synthetic content.
The incentive shift favors human authorship: AI is welcome as assistance, not as the sole creator.

items.title: Radiologists defied automation predictions
points: Despite AI advances and cheaper imaging, demand for radiologists stayed strong.
AI experts had predicted obsolescence for the profession by 2021.

items.title: Surfsense: open-source NotebookLM rival
points: Searches Reddit, YouTube, TikTok, and Google Maps live to build searchable knowledge bases.
Every result comes with its source attached, and self-hosted deployment is offered.

items.title: Practical guides: better prompts and 20 AI terms in 40 minutes
points: Zapier's guide covers four techniques: prompt skeletons (templates with blanks to fill), worked examples (showing the correct output format), chained steps (breaking a task into a sequence), and meta-prompting (asking the AI to write its own prompt first).

A 40-minute video explains 20 AI terms including tokens (discrete units of text a model processes), attention (the mechanism deciding which words matter most), RAG (retrieval-augmented generation: fetching external data before answering), agents (autonomous multi-step programs), and quantization (compressing model size).
The common thread is specificity: examples train output format, step-by-step reasoning makes complex asks debuggable, and meta-prompting surfaces hidden assumptions.

issues.subject: 🦾 10 Ways to Get Better AI Answers

headlines: Suno AI music generator lost a German copyright case and must pay damages; the court found it processed songs without authorization, marking a potential global precedent as the company plans appeal.
Google's Gemini Spark now automates tasks inside Chrome—it can book apartment viewings, research flights, and start bookings using your logged-in accounts with your permission.

Four platforms including Snapchat are now blocking AI-generated videos from recommendations, though human-edited content with AI assistance still appears; a shift driven by user backlash against AI-only content.
Radiologists defied predictions of automation; despite AI advances and cheaper imaging, demand for radiologists remained strong instead of the obsolescence AI experts predicted by 2021.
Surfsense, an open-source NotebookLM rival, searches Reddit, YouTube, TikTok, and Google Maps live—building searchable knowledge bases with every source attached and offering self-hosted options.

sections.title: Gemini Spark Becomes Your Personal Errand Runner
points: 1. Google now lets Gemini Spark access your saved passwords and logged-in accounts to complete real tasks: booking apartments, researching and starting flight bookings, and handing payment decisions back to you.
2. The feature requires explicit permission but reduces the friction between researching something in AI and actually booking it—no manual re-entry of details across different sites.
3. This is deployment of AI agents (software that takes multi-step actions autonomously) into consumer Chrome workflows, where previously such tasks required manual tab-switching and form-filling.

sections.title: Platform Crackdown on Pure AI-Generated Content
points: 1. Snapchat's Spotlight now deprioritizes wholly AI-generated videos in recommendations while still allowing videos that humans created and AI edited.
2. Four platforms moved within two weeks, signaling a market shift toward protecting human creators or perceived user fatigue with obvious synthetic content.
3. The distinction matters: AI tools are welcome as assistance, but feeds will favor human authorship, reshaping incentives for creators to at least initiate content themselves.

sections.title: Suno's Copyright Loss and Global Implications
points: 1. A Munich court ordered Suno AI to pay damages for processing songs the company had no right to use during training, finding copyright violation regardless of AI's generative purpose.
2. Gema, the German rights organization, called it 'a verdict of global significance'—suggesting the ruling could influence how courts worldwide treat AI training on copyrighted material.
3. Suno plans to appeal, but the decision establishes legal precedent that AI music generators cannot freely consume copyrighted works to build capability without licensing.

sections.title: How to Extract Better Answers from AI Systems
points: 1. Zapier's guide covers four techniques: prompt skeletons (templates with blanks to fill), worked examples (showing correct output format), chained steps (breaking tasks into sequence), and meta-prompting (asking the AI to write its own prompt first).

2. A 40-minute video explains 20 AI terms—tokens (discrete units of text the model processes), attention (the mechanism deciding which words matter most), RAG (retrieval-augmented generation: fetching external data before answering), agents (autonomous multi-step programs), and quantization (compressing model size)—so hype cycles lose power over you.

3. Improvement comes from specificity: skeleton prompts reduce ambiguity, examples train the model's output format, step-by-step reasoning breaks complex asks into debuggable pieces, and asking the AI to articulate its own instructions surfaces hidden assumptions.
